steps.text: This seems like enough information, and nothing concerning about it.

submission.reasoning: svchost.exe, running from its normal path C:\windows\system32, opened lsass.exe on workstation5 six times between 06:36:43 and 06:36:44. The access mask was 0x1000 (PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION), which lets a process read basic details but not LSASS memory, so it cannot be used to dump credentials. The call trace runs from RPC dispatch (RPCRT4.dll) through lsm.dll, the Local Session Manager service, which matches normal session-management queries. The source process has no other suspicious relations in the graph. I did not check its command line, parent process or user account. Assessed as normal Windows OS activity.
